sell_stone_1.name: Chipped Ostracon
sell_stone_1.description: A broken pottery shard scratched with a scribe's practice notes — worthless to read, but Fez pays for the clay.

sell_stone_2.name: Cracked Clay Jar
sell_stone_2.description: A storage jar for grain or beer, split down one side by the weight of centuries.

sell_stone_3.name: Worn Reed Sandal
sell_stone_3.description: Woven from papyrus reeds, the sole worn thin by some long-forgotten worker's daily walk.

sell_stone_4.name: Faded Linen Scrap
sell_stone_4.description: A torn strip of undyed linen, the kind wound endlessly around the dead — or used to patch a sail.

sell_stone_5.name: Broken Flint Blade
sell_stone_5.description: A knapped flint knife, snapped at the tip. Cheap to make, cheaper to replace.

sell_bronze_1.name: Bent Bronze Amulet
sell_bronze_1.description: A cheap protective charm, cast crooked and never fixed. Common enough that no collector wants it — but bronze is bronze.

sell_bronze_2.name: Corroded Bronze Mirror
sell_bronze_2.description: Once polished bright enough to see your reflection; now clouded green with age.

sell_bronze_3.name: Dull Bronze Fishhook
sell_bronze_3.description: A fisherman's tool, lost overboard on the Nile long before the tomb was sealed.

sell_bronze_4.name: Small Bronze Bell
sell_bronze_4.description: Meant to hang from a temple door or a dancer's ankle — it no longer rings true.

sell_bronze_5.name: Tarnished Bronze Ring
sell_bronze_5.description: A plain band, sized for a finger long since turned to dust.

sell_silver_1.name: Tarnished Silver Ankh
sell_silver_1.description: A symbol of life, worn dull by centuries underground. Too tarnished to display, still worth its weight.

sell_silver_2.name: Silver Kohl Applicator
sell_silver_2.description: A slender rod once used to line the eyes of the wealthy — the kohl is long gone.

sell_silver_3.name: Dented Silver Bowl
sell_silver_3.description: A small offering bowl, crushed on one side when the ceiling above it finally gave way.

sell_silver_4.name: Silver Hair Pin
sell_silver_4.description: Simple and unadorned, it once held back the hair of someone whose name is lost.

sell_silver_5.name: Worn Silver Bracelet
sell_silver_5.description: A thin band of silver, its clasp broken. Not fine enough for a noble, too fine for a laborer.

sell_gold_1.name: Small Gold Bead
sell_gold_1.description: One bead from a burial necklace, scattered long ago. A jeweler's delight, if you can find the rest.

sell_gold_2.name: Gold Leaf Fragment
sell_gold_2.description: A sliver of gold leaf, peeled from a statue's face by grave robbers centuries before you arrived.

sell_gold_3.name: Thin Gold Earring
sell_gold_3.description: Hammered thin to stretch a noble's gold further — still enough to catch a merchant's eye.

sell_gold_4.name: Gold-Flecked Shard
sell_gold_4.description: A broken piece of gilded plaster, flecks of real gold still clinging to the surface.

sell_gold_5.name: Chipped Gold Signet
sell_gold_5.description: A seal ring, its engraving worn past recognition — whoever it named is forgotten.

sell_divine_1.name: Faded Lapis Scarab
sell_divine_1.description: Carved from precious lapis lazuli, imported at great cost for a pharaoh's rebirth. The color has faded, the value hasn't.

sell_divine_2.name: Carnelian Eye Amulet
sell_divine_2.description: A protective eye carved from blood-red carnelian, meant to ward off misfortune in the afterlife.

sell_divine_3.name: Turquoise Inlay Chip
sell_divine_3.description: A single tile from a shattered mosaic, once part of a god's likeness on a temple wall.

sell_divine_4.name: Alabaster Canopic Shard
sell_divine_4.description: A broken piece of a jar meant to hold a pharaoh's preserved organs — precious stone for a grim purpose.

sell_divine_5.name: Obsidian Ritual Blade
sell_divine_5.description: Volcanic glass, ground to a ceremonial edge never meant for battle — only for the temple.
